context.why: US-2 registered PortalRolePermissionBackend and it derives an object-level answer from EVERY model-level permission a person holds, including one granted directly to that person. That reopened a hole an earlier feature deliberately closed: four pre-existing tests assert that somebody holding dataset.change_dataset or project.change_project directly, with no grant on the record, is refused on a private record's update, delete and descriptions pages. All four now fail. The implementer was right to leave them alone and escalate. The rule is what needs narrowing, not the tests. The approved specification requires a ROLE's rights to reach records (FR-003, FR-018, FR-020). It never asked for a permission granted directly to a person to do so, and that wider reading was mine, written into the plan before this collision was known. Narrow the backend to permissions held through one of the four shipped portal roles. A Data Curator still changes any dataset; a person carrying a stray direct grant is refused exactly as they were before this feature. That also removes the breaking change for existing portals, so the upgrade note US-1 wrote is no longer true and has to be rewritten.
spec_sections: Requirements / How rights are decided (FR-018, FR-020)
prior_decisions: D20 (this feature's decisions.md, written by the previous implementer) records the collision, the four failing tests, and that reverting the AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS entry makes them pass. Read it. Your job is the narrowing it could not choose on its own authority.

The earlier feature's guard is evidence about intent, not an obstacle: a page relying on an inherited visibility rule is not guarded at all, which is why those four tests exist. Do not modify, weaken, skip or delete any of them - after your change they must pass unchanged.
D14 - the exclusion for contributors.manage_organization stays exactly as it is.

Research R2's reasoning still holds for the role case: ModelBackend answers False for every object-level question, so without this backend a Data Curator holding change_dataset cannot change a dataset. What changes is the SOURCE of the permission the backend will honour.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a person in the Data Curator role, When has_perm('dataset.change_dataset', any_dataset) is asked, Then True - including for a private dataset they have no record-level grant on. Given a person holding dataset.change_dataset directly through user_permissions and in no portal role, When the same question is asked, Then False. Given a person in a group the portal created itself that carries dataset.change_dataset, When the same question is asked, Then False - only the four shipped roles confer this. Given obj is None, an anonymous user, a deactivated account, or contributors.manage_organization, Then False, exactly as now. And the four pre-existing tests in tests/test_core/test_dataset/test_plugins.py and tests/test_core/test_project/test_plugins.py pass unchanged.
